name: Vitoria
summary: Wellington caught King Joseph's three armies in the basin of Vitoria with their backs to the Pyrenees. Hill attacked over the La Puebla heights in the south, the centre columns crossed the Zadorra by its bridges, and Graham came down on the French line of retreat from the north. The French broke, abandoning their guns, their baggage and the treasure of a kingdom, and fled for France.

sources.label: Battle of Vitoria order of battle (Wikipedia)

forces.name: Stewart's 2nd Division
forces.summary: Opened the battle on the right, storming the heights of La Puebla with Morillo's Spaniards and holding them against Gazan's counter-attacks.
notes: Cadogan's brigade had two Highland battalions, the 71st and 92nd, where the list allows one in four, which shows as a historical departure. Cadogan was killed on the heights.
Each brigade had a company of the 5/60th; one is shown, the list allowing one in an army.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Silveira's Portuguese Division
forces.summary: Hill's Portuguese division, following the 2nd Division along the Puebla heights and the valley below.
notes: Without British brigades for its Portuguese ones to go with, the list's ratio shows as a historical departure. Tulloh's two Portuguese batteries are shown as one.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Morillo's Spanish Division
forces.summary: Led the climb onto the heights of La Puebla and fought for them all morning; Morillo was wounded.
notes: The order of battle lists the division's regiments without brigades or battalion counts; one battalion each, in two brigades.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but First Brigade at 7, the most the list allows; Second Brigade at 7, the most the list allows.

forces.name: Cole's 4th Division
forces.summary: Crossed the Zadorra at Nanclares and pushed into the French centre around Ariñez as the line gave way.
notes: Skerrett's company of the Brunswick Oels is left out, the list allowing one such company in an army.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Light Division
forces.summary: Guided over the unguarded bridge at Tres Puentes, it got across the Zadorra behind the French centre and opened the way for the rest.
notes: The list allows horse artillery by the cavalry taken, so a horse troop with an infantry division shows as a historical departure.
Wellington rode with the centre, so the book's named Wellington leads it here; Alten commanded the division.
Two Light Brigades where the list takes one show as a historical departure. The order of battle names no commander for the 1st Brigade; Kempt led it at the bridge.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Sir Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington, with his own rating.

forces.name: Picton's 3rd Division
forces.summary: Tired of waiting for Dalhousie, Picton led his division over the bridge of Mendoza and into the French centre, carrying the knoll of Ariñez.
notes: The list allows one Highland or Light battalion in four, so a brigade of three may have none; where one had a Highland or Light regiment, that shows as a historical departure.
Picton is the book's named commander.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Major-General Sir Thomas Picton, with his own rating.

forces.name: Dalhousie's 7th Division
forces.summary: Came up late through the hills and crossed the Zadorra behind Picton to join the attack on the French centre.
notes: Grant's brigade had two Light battalions in four where the list allows one, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Howard's 1st Division
forces.summary: With Graham's column, which came down on the French right and the Bayonne road, their line of retreat, around Gamarra.
notes: The Guards Brigade comes with two British or KGL brigades in the list, and here there's one, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Oswald's 5th Division
forces.summary: Stormed the village of Gamarra Mayor and fought for its bridge against Reille's Army of Portugal, closing the road to France.
notes: Robinson's company of the Brunswick Oels is left out, the list allowing one such company in an army.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Pack's and Bradford's Portuguese
forces.summary: Graham's two independent Portuguese brigades, which led the attack on the heights before Gamarra and Abechuco.
notes: Without British brigades for the Portuguese ones to go with, the list's ratio shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Longa's Spanish Division
forces.summary: Longa's Cantabrians seized the bridge at Durana on the Bayonne road, cutting the French off from their best line of retreat.
notes: One battalion each, in two brigades; the Húsares de Iberia and Salcedo's guerrillas are left out.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but First Brigade at 7, the most the list allows; Second Brigade at 7, the most the list allows.

forces.name: The Heavy Cavalry
forces.formation: Hill's Household, Ponsonby's, Fane's and Bock's brigades
forces.summary: Waiting through the morning for the infantry to open the way, the heavy brigades crossed the Zadorra in the afternoon and pressed the French as they broke.
notes: The Household brigade had no Dragoon regiments, which the list's heavy brigade needs, and cavalry alone has no infantry brigades for its brigades to go with; these show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: The Light Cavalry
forces.formation: Grant's, Alten's, Anson's and D'Urban's brigades
forces.summary: Grant's hussars and the light dragoons pursued the broken French past Vitoria, where many stopped to plunder the abandoned baggage train.
notes: Cavalry on its own has no infantry brigades for its brigades to go with, which shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Leval's Division
forces.summary: Held the French front line south of the Zadorra until the centre was turned, and fell back with the Army of the South.
notes: No source gives the battalions of each French regiment in 1813; two each, as the divisions' strengths suggest, is how they're shown.
